class WilsonLoop¶
#include <WilsonLoop.h>

Wilson loop observable on a triangulated spacetime.

Computes holonomy-like quantities around closed paths. The dual-graph modes (top-simplices as nodes, shared facets as edges) let users choose between purely combinatorial, curvature-based, and causal-structure analyses. The U1_CONNECTION mode instead accumulates the U(1) connection (Edge::phase) around a cycle on the primal 1-skeleton, returning the gauge-invariant holonomy (mod 2π) — the Wilson-loop view of the Stage-1 cobordism::HodgeLaplacian cycle flux.

Usage: 

auto wl = WilsonLoop(spacetime);
auto loop = wl.hingeLoop(some_hinge);
auto result = wl.evaluate(loop, WilsonMode::DEFICIT_ANGLE);

U(1) connection holonomy around a closed cycle of vertices on the primal 1-skeleton.

Accumulates Edge::phase oriented along the stored source→target direction (+phase forward, −phase on reversal) and reduces the total into the principal interval (−π, π]. value carries the holonomy; loopSize the number of edges. Returns an empty result if the cycle has fewer than two vertices or any consecutive pair is not joined by an edge (an open path).

This is the Wilson-loop counterpart of the Stage-1 cycle flux carried by the Hermitian-weighted cobordism::HodgeLaplacian (the same oriented phase sum); restricted to phases in {0, π} it reproduces the ℤ₂ flux.

template<typename OnCycleFn>
void bfsFindCycles(SimplexPtr start, int maxDepth, int minCurDepth, OnCycleFn onCycle) const¶

BFS over the dual graph starting at start, yielding each cycle to onCycle(path).

The path runs start → … → start. If onCycle returns true, the walk terminates; otherwise it continues searching.

maxDepth < 0 disables the depth cap. minCurDepth filters out cycles whose far endpoint is too close to the start (used by the target-length search to skip trivial back-and-forth cycles of length 2).

Shared implementation backing both geodesicLoop (first cycle, no depth cap) and dualLatticeLoop (best target-length cycle within a depth budget).

class ModularityOptimizer¶
#include <ModularityOptimizer.h>

Modularity sweep on a CDT spacetime, driven by transactional Pachner moves with Q-direction acceptance.

Algorithm (per iteration):

  1. Pick a random move type from {add, remove, flip, iflip, shift}.

  2. cdt.proposeXxx() — read-only target selection. If no eligible target, try another move type (one fallback each iteration).

  3. Snapshot Q on the spacetime 1-skeleton.

  4. move.apply() — commit the move.

  5. Compute Q after. If direction matches (up: Q rose; down: Q fell), keep the move. Otherwise move.rollback().

  6. If Q crossed the next target_dq threshold, build the dual graph and measure D_S; record a Measurement.

The “informed proposal” hook in selectMoveType can bias the move-type distribution toward those most likely to move Q in the target direction. Default: uniform over all 5 types.

class SparseGraph : public SpectralGraph¶
#include <SparseGraph.h>

Undirected sparse graph in CSR (compressed sparse row) form.

Built from a (rows, cols) COO array — typically from :func:Spacetime::getDualAdjacency for the modularity / spectral- dimension observables. All operations are read-only on the graph data; the modularity sweep recomputes the graph from the spacetime at every measurement rather than mutating it.

Derives from SpectralGraph, inheriting the diagonal heat-kernel and return-probability machinery; the override here installs the symmetric normalised Laplacian L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}.

No Eigen dependency — plain std::vector storage so this header is cheap to include from anywhere in tessera_core.

void applyLaplacian(std::vector<double> const &x, std::vector<double> &y) const override¶

y ← L_sym · x where L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2}.

Isolated nodes (degree 0) get invSqrtDeg = 0, so the matvec reduces to y_i = x_i — L_sym acts as the identity on them.

bool isBipartite() const¶

True iff the graph is 2-colorable (no odd cycle).

BFS-based; empty graphs are trivially bipartite.

std::vector<double> diagonalHeatKernel(const std::vector<std::uint32_t> &starts, const std::vector<double> &times, int krylovDim = 30) const¶

Diagonal of the heat kernel e^{-t L_sym} for each (start, t) pair.

Returns a flat row-major matrix of shape (starts.size(), times.size()). out[w][j] is the approximated [e^{-times[j] L_sym}]_{starts[w], starts[w]}.

Implemented as a thin uint32_t-keyed wrapper around the inherited SpectralGraph::diagonalHeatKernel so that the Python binding keeps its existing list-of-unsigned-index signature, and the nEdges_ == 0 fast path stays here (empty-graph return = 1.0 by convention).

Note: L_rw = I - D^{-1} A (random-walk Laplacian) and L_sym = I - D^{-1/2} A D^{-1/2} (symmetric normalized) are related by L_rw = D^{-1/2} L_sym D^{1/2}. Their diagonal entries of e^{-tL} are identical (D^{1/2} D^{-1/2} = I on the diagonal) — so D_S extraction gives the same answer with either, and L_sym is symmetric, which lets us use the cheap Lanczos rather than Arnoldi.

std::pair<double, double> spectralDimension(int nWalks, double maxSigma, std::mt19937 *rng, double tailFraction = 0.2, int nTimes = 40, double tMin = 0.5, int krylovDim = 30) const¶

Estimate the spectral dimension at small and large diffusion times via a centered finite-difference of -2 d log K(t) / d log t.

Mirrors the Python implementation in examples/modularity.py:spectral_dimension.

Picks nWalks random start nodes uniformly without replacement (capped at nNodes()).

Returns (D_S_small, D_S_large) as a pair, or {NaN, NaN} if the graph is too small or has no valid log-K samples.

Note this overload returns a (small, large) pair via random-walk sampling, distinct from the inherited static SpectralGraph::spectralDimension(sigmas, P) which is a pure finite-difference helper on a precomputed P(σ) curve.

class Cobordism¶
#include <Cobordism.h>

Cobordism verification¶

A cobordism from one manifold \( M_1 \) to another \( M_2 \) is a higher-dimensional manifold \( W \) whose boundary is exactly the two of them placed side by side ( \( \partial W = M_1 \sqcup M_2 \)). For example a solid cylinder is a cobordism from a circle to a circle, and a solid disk is a cobordism from a circle to “nothing” (the empty manifold).

This class checks whether a given \( W \) really is such a cobordism. It is a static-only utility (no state) operating on triangulations (Spacetimes). This first version checks the boundary structure: that the boundary of \( W \) breaks into connected pieces that match \( M_1 \) and \( M_2 \) as triangulations, plus the basic chain-complex sanity check that the boundary of the boundary is empty. The two further checks the full specification calls for — that \( W \) is a genuine manifold (every vertex’s neighborhood looks like a ball or sphere) and that the boundary’s orientation is consistent — are separate follow-ups.

Returned as sorted vertex-id tuples. An interior face belongs to two top simplices and is excluded; a boundary face belongs to just one.

static CobordismResult verify(const Spacetime &W, const Spacetime &M1, const Spacetime &M2)¶

Verify that \( W \) is a cobordism from \( M_1 \) to \( M_2 \): its boundary splits into connected pieces that are, up to relabeling, the triangulations \( M_1 \) and \( M_2 \) (either of which may be the empty manifold).

Also checks the boundary-of-a-boundary is empty.

static std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> glue(const Spacetime &W1, const Spacetime &W2)¶

Gluing (composition of cobordisms)¶

Form the composite \( W_2 \cup_{\Sigma_C} W_1 \) of two cobordisms that share a boundary surface \( \Sigma_C \): a boundary component of \( W_1 \) that is isomorphic (as a triangulation) to one of \( W_2 \). The two copies of \( \Sigma_C \) are identified vertex-for-vertex by the order-preserving simplicial isomorphism between them (the same correspondence areIsomorphic certifies), the two complexes are reindexed into one dense vertex range, and their top simplices are merged. The glued \( \Sigma_C \) faces, now shared by one top simplex from each side, become interior; the result’s boundary is the remaining components \( \partial W_1 \sqcup \partial W_2 \) with the two \( \Sigma_C \) copies removed. Returned as a fresh pre-geometric Spacetime ready for DijkgraafWitten. The first isomorphic pair (in the deterministic component order) is used as \( \Sigma_C \).

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if either input is empty, the top dimensions differ, or no shared boundary surface exists.

static std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> disjointUnion(const Spacetime &W1, const Spacetime &W2)¶

Disjoint union (the disconnected cobordism)¶

The disjoint union \( W_1 \sqcup W_2 \) of two triangulations: \( W_2 \)‘s vertices are shifted into a fresh id range above \( W_1 \)‘s so the two complexes share no vertex, and their top simplices are concatenated into a single Spacetime. Nothing is identified, so \( \partial(W_1\sqcup W_2) = \partial W_1 \sqcup \partial W_2 \) and the bulk is disconnected. Two solid tori \( S^1\times D^2 \) (each \( \partial = T^2 \)) thus give a bulk with \( \partial W = T^2 \sqcup T^2 \): the cap-and-create cobordism \( T^2 \to T^2 \) that is not a mapping cylinder. Its DW map factorizes over the components to the rank-1 outer product \( |st\rangle\langle st| \) ( \( |st\rangle \) the solid-torus boundary state) — a non-invertible boundary map, unreachable by any cylinder (whose map is always an invertible permutation). The result is a fresh pre-geometric Spacetime ready for DijkgraafWitten::map(), whose two-component requirement it satisfies while the bulk need not be connected.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if either input is empty or the two top dimensions differ.

static std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> selfGlue(const Spacetime &W)¶

Close a cobordism by gluing its two boundary components to each other (the categorical trace / mapping torus): \( \partial W \) must have exactly two isomorphic components \( \Sigma_C^{(0)}, \Sigma_C^{(1)} \), which are identified by the order-preserving isomorphism, yielding a closed manifold.

The collar must be thick enough that no single top simplex touches both components (a top simplex spanning both would gain a repeated vertex on identification); e.g. \( T^2\times[0,T] \) needs at least three layers in the \( [0,T] \) direction so the glued circle is a non-degenerate triangulation.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if \( \partial W \) does not have exactly two isomorphic components; std::runtime_error if the identification collapses a top simplex (collar too thin).

static std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> twistedCylinder(const Spacetime &sigma, const std::vector<std::uint64_t> &phi)¶

Twisted cylinder (a non-identity DW boundary map)¶

The \( \varphi \)-twisted product cobordism \( \Sigma\times[0,T] : \Sigma \to \Sigma \), whose two boundary copies of the surface \( \Sigma \) are threaded through a finite-order simplicial automorphism \( \varphi \) of the triangulated \( \Sigma \). The ordinary product cylinder — the one glue/selfGlue produce, identified by the order-preserving (identity) isomorphism — has DW map the identity on \( Z(\Sigma) \); that identity identification is the single home of the “\f$ \to I \f$” collapse. Putting \( \varphi \) there instead makes the interior monodromy from the bottom boundary to the top boundary equal \( \varphi \), so DijkgraafWitten::map() returns the permutation \( \varphi \) induces on the holonomy classes \( Z(\Sigma)=\mathbb{C}[H^1(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}_2)] \). For the coordinate-swap \( \varphi:(x,y)\mapsto(y,x) \) of a square-product torus \( T^2=S^1\times S^1 \) this transposes the holonomy classes \( [a]\leftrightarrow[b] \) while fixing \( [0] \) and \( [a{+}b] \) — a non-identity \( 4\times4 \) permutation ( \( \varphi\bmod 2 \) is the modular \( S=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) \)).

Construction: three stacked copies of \( \Sigma \) (levels 0,1,2 at vertex ids \( x,\;|V|{+}x,\;2|V|{+}x \)). The level-0 prism is the ordinary Eilenberg–Zilber product \( \Sigma\times[0,1] \) (the same staircase SimplicialProduct uses); the level-1 prism is the same product but its lower face is glued to the shared seam through \( \varphi \) (the level-1 vertex of \( \varphi(x) \) carries the seam id of \( x \)). Because \( \varphi \) is a simplicial automorphism the two prisms induce the same triangulation on the seam, so it closes up; the seam (level 1) is interior, and \( \partial W \) is the two \( \Sigma \) copies at levels 0 and 2 ( \( \geq 3 \) layers, so no top simplex touches both boundaries). The result is a fresh pre-geometric Spacetime ready for DijkgraafWitten::map().

\( \varphi \) of order \( n \) gives a DW map of order \( n \) (map \( {}^n=I \)), and composing twists composes the permutations — the functoriality of the DW functor. Only the finite-order modular elements (orders 2,3,4,6) are realizable this way: the Dehn twist \( T=\bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr) \) is infinite-order, hence not a finite-order simplicial automorphism of any fixed triangulation — which is exactly why a fixed-triangulation cobordism could only ever realize the identity until now.

Parameters:

  • sigma – a closed triangulated surface \( \Sigma \) whose vertices are exactly \( 0..|V|-1 \) (as the product-torus fixtures produce).

  • phi – a vertex permutation (phi[x] is the image of vertex \( x \)) that is a simplicial automorphism of \( \Sigma \) — both validated.

Throws:

std::invalid_argument – if \( \Sigma \) is not a 2-dimensional triangulation with vertices \( 0..|V|-1 \), or phi is not a length- \( |V| \) permutation, or phi is not a simplicial automorphism of \( \Sigma \) (some top triangle’s image is not a triangle).

class ChainComplex¶
#include <ChainComplex.h>

ChainComplex¶

The simplicial chain complex of a triangulation: the boundary maps ∂_k : C_k → C_{k-1} over ℤ, plus the homology invariants derived from them (Betti numbers over ℤ and ℤ/2, torsion coefficients) and the ∂²=0 sanity check. Purely combinatorial — built from the vertex sets of the complex, independent of any geometry.

Simplices are enumerated as the full face-closure of the complex’s simplices (every sub-face of every registered simplex). Each k-simplex is identified by its sorted vertex-id tuple and assigned an index; its reference orientation is the increasing-vertex-id ordering, so ∂[v_0 < … < v_k] = Σ_i (−1)^i [v_0,…,v̂_i,…,v_k].

Public Functions

inline int dimension() const noexcept¶

Top dimension n (largest k with a k-simplex), or -1 if empty.

std::size_t numSimplices(int k) const noexcept¶

|C_k|, the number of k-simplices (0 if k out of range).

inline const std::vector<std::size_t> &fVector() const noexcept¶

f-vector (|C_0|, …, |C_n|).

int eulerCharacteristic() const noexcept¶

Euler characteristic χ = Σ_k (−1)^k |C_k|.

const std::vector<long> &boundaryMatrix(int k) const¶

The boundary matrix ∂_k (rows = |C_{k-1}|, cols = |C_k|), flat row-major.

Entries in {−1, 0, +1}. ∂_0 is empty. Out-of-range k returns an empty matrix.

bool boundaryComposesToZero() const¶

Check ∂_{k-1} ∘ ∂_k = 0 for all k (chain-complex axiom / V3 sanity check).

std::vector<int> bettiNumbers() const¶

Betti numbers b_0..b_n over ℚ (free ranks of H_k): b_k = |C_k| − rank ∂_k − rank ∂_{k+1}.

std::vector<int> bettiNumbersGF2() const¶

Betti numbers over GF(2): b_k = |C_k| − rank₂ ∂_k − rank₂ ∂_{k+1}.

std::vector<long> torsion(int k) const¶

Torsion coefficients of \( H_k \): the invariant factors \( > 1 \) of \( \partial_{k+1} \).

(E.g. \( \mathbb{RP}^2 \) has \( \mathrm{torsion}(1) = \{2\} \).)

std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> kSimplexVertices(int k) const¶

The k-simplices as sorted vertex-id tuples, in the canonical order of \( C_k \) — the column order of \( \partial_{k+1} \) and, equally, the row order of \( \partial_k \).

For \( k = \) dimension() this is orientedTopSimplices(); for \( k = 1 \) it is the edge ordering the rows of boundaryMatrix(2) refer to, which is needed to read a \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) connection \( g \in C^1 \) on a simplex’s edges. Empty when \( k \) is out of range.

std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> orientedTopSimplices() const¶

The top simplices as sorted vertex-id tuples, in the canonical column order of the top boundary matrix \( \partial_d \) ( \( d = \) dimension()).

This is the ordering the orientation signs from fundamentalClass() refer to. Empty for the empty complex.

std::vector<int> fundamentalClass() const¶

The fundamental class \( [W] \in H_d \) of a closed oriented \( d \)-manifold: the per top-simplex orientation signs \( \varepsilon_t = \pm 1 \) (indexed as orientedTopSimplices(), i.e.

the columns of \( \partial_d \)) that make the top chain \( \sum_t \varepsilon_t\, t \) a cycle ( \( \partial_d \sum_t \varepsilon_t\, t = 0 \), so each codimension-one face’s two incident top simplices cancel). It is the \( \pm 1 \) generator of \( \ker \partial_d \), which is one-dimensional ( \( b_d = 1 \)) for a closed connected oriented manifold, hence unique up to an overall sign; the sign is fixed deterministically by making the first nonzero entry \( +1 \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if no such class exists — the complex is not a closed connected oriented \( d \)-manifold ( \( \dim \ker \partial_d \neq 1 \)) — or \( d < 1 \).

std::vector<double> intersectionForm() const¶

The symmetric intersection form \( Q_{ij} = \langle \alpha_i \cup \alpha_j, [K] \rangle \) on a basis \( \{\alpha_i\} \) of the free part of \( H^2 \), as a flat row-major \( b_2 \times b_2 \) matrix.

Defined for a closed oriented 4-manifold ( \( n = 4 \)); the cup product is the Alexander–Whitney product evaluated on the fundamental class \( [K] \) (the generator of \( \ker \partial_4 \)). Empty when \( n \neq 4 \) or \( b_2 = 0 \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if \( n = 4 \), \( b_2 > 0 \), but the complex is not closed-orientable (no fundamental class).

int signature() const¶

Signature \( \sigma = b_+ - b_- \) of the intersection form (Sylvester inertia).

0 when \( n \neq 4 \) or \( b_2 = 0 \).

std::map<std::string, int> stiefelWhitneyNumbers() const¶

Mod-2 Stiefel–Whitney numbers of a closed PL \( n \)-manifold: \( \langle w_{i_1}\cdots w_{i_r}, [K] \rangle \in \mathbb{Z}/2 \) for every partition \( (i_1,\dots,i_r) \) of \( n \) into positive parts, keyed by the monomial (e.g.

"w4", "w2^2", "w1^2", "w1w3"). Empty when the complex is empty.

Computed combinatorially: the mod-2 cohomology \( H^*(K;\mathbb{Z}/2) \) (from the boundary maps reduced mod 2), the Alexander–Whitney cup product on cochains, and the Wu classes \( v_k \) — defined by \( \langle v_k \cup x, [K]\rangle = \langle \mathrm{Sq}^k x, [K]\rangle \) for all \( x \in H^{n-k} \) — from which the total Stiefel–Whitney class is \( w = \mathrm{Sq}(v) \). The fundamental class \( [K] \) over \( \mathbb{Z}/2 \) is the sum of all top simplices, and evaluation on it is the mod-2 sum of a top-degree cochain over those simplices.

Only the Steenrod squares expressible through the ordinary ( \( \cup_0 \)) product are implemented: \( \mathrm{Sq}^k \) on a class of degree \( k \) (the squaring) and the degree-forced zeros. These suffice for surfaces and for closed orientable 4-manifolds with \( b_1 = 0 \) (so \( \mathbb{RP}^2 \), \( \mathbb{CP}^2 \), \( S^4 \), \( S^2\times S^2 \), and their disjoint unions).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if a required Wu or Stiefel–Whitney class genuinely needs a higher cup- \( i \) product ( \( i>0 \)) — the general Steenrod squares are deferred (see issue #65).

class HodgeLaplacian¶
#include <HodgeLaplacian.h>

HodgeLaplacian¶

The Hodge Laplacian on a Spacetime, degree-parameterized by int k.

At \( k = 0 \) it is the Hermitian U(1)-weighted graph Laplacian \( L = D - A \) on the 1-skeleton, assembled directly from the complex edge weights \( \text{squaredLength}\cdot e^{i\,\text{phase}} \) carried by each Edge (the magnitude convention on the degree keeps \( L \) Hermitian and \( e^{-iLt} \) unitary). This path is unchanged.

At \( k \geq 1 \) it is the metric Hodge Laplacian, assembled from the integer boundary maps \( \partial_k,\partial_{k+1} \) (ChainComplex) and the diagonal inner-product weights \( W_k \) — the per- \( k \)-simplex Euclidean volumes (Simplex::volume), with \( W_0 = I \). With the metric adjoint \( \partial_k^* = W_k^{-1}\partial_k^{\top} W_{k-1} \) the Laplacian is \( L_k = \partial_k^*\partial_k + \partial_{k+1}\partial_{k+1}^* \), returned in its symmetric ( \( W_k \)-orthonormal) representation \( W_k^{1/2} L_k W_k^{-1/2} = B_k^{\top}B_k + B_{k+1}B_{k+1}^{\top} \) with \( B_k = W_{k-1}^{1/2}\partial_k W_k^{-1/2} \) — symmetric positive semidefinite, so SelfAdjointEigenSolver applies and the spectrum/kernel are those of \( L_k \) (a similarity). By the discrete Hodge theorem \( \ker L_k \cong H_k \), so \( \dim\ker L_k = b_k \) for any positive weights; passing metric = false uses unit weights — the combinatorial \( \partial_k^{\top}\partial_k + \partial_{k+1}\partial_{k+1}^{\top} \) — as a same-kernel cross-check. A negative \( k \) throws; a \( k \) beyond the top dimension has no \( k \)-cells and yields empty results.

Lorentzian d’Alembertian (§5.6)¶

The lorentzian = true path keeps the same metric-Hodge construction but weights \( W_k \) with the signed Simplex::volume() — the honest, signature-respecting content in which a timelike edge ( \( l^2 < 0 \)) carries a negative volume — instead of \( |\text{volume}| \). The inner product then goes indefinite: the symmetric \( W_k^{1/2} \) similarity breaks (the square root of a negative weight is imaginary), so the operator \( L_k = \partial_k^*\partial_k + \partial_{k+1}\partial_{k+1}^* \) with the signed metric adjoint \( \partial_k^* = W_k^{-1}\partial_k^{\top}W_{k-1} \) is assembled directly — \( L_k = W_k^{-1}\partial_k^{\top}W_{k-1}\partial_k + \partial_{k+1}W_{k+1}^{-1}\partial_{k+1}^{\top}W_k \) — and is generally non-self-adjoint (a discrete d’Alembertian). It is diagonalized with a general Eigen::EigenSolver, so eigenvalues may be negative or complex. The clean \( \ker L_k \cong H_k \) degrades to a pseudo-Hodge decomposition: “harmonic” becomes the small- \( |\lambda| \) near-kernel, and a near-kernel representative \( h \) may be null in the indefinite metric ( \( \langle h,h\rangle_W = \sum_i W_{k,i}|h_i|^2 \approx 0 \)). When every \( l^2 > 0 \) the signed content equals \( |\text{volume}| \) and this path reproduces the Euclidean spectrum/kernel above. The Euclidean (lorentzian = false) path is untouched.

For \( k = 0 \) vertices are indexed by a stable order (sorted vertex id \( \to 0..N-1 \)); for \( k \geq 1 \) the \( k \)-cells follow the canonical ChainComplex column order (sorted vertex-id tuples), so the returned flat row-major matrices are reproducible and align with boundaryMatrix(k) and weights(k).

Assembly (k = 0)¶

  • Adjacency \( A_{ij} = \sum_{(i,j)} \text{squaredLength}\cdot e^{i\,\text{phase}} \), summed over edges between \( i \) and \( j \); the stored source→target orientation carries \( +\text{phase} \), the reverse carries \( -\text{phase} \), so \( A = A^\dagger \) (Hermitian).

  • Degree \( D_{ii} = \sum |\text{squaredLength}| \) over incident edges (the magnitude convention — keeps \( L \) Hermitian and \( e^{-iLt} \) unitary for complex weights).

  • Laplacian \( L = D - A \).

This class is the operator only: it does not compute fluxes, cycle bases, or Betti numbers (those are WilsonLoop / ChainComplex’s job), and it does not gauge-transform the mesh (gauge invariance is exercised by rephasing the edges and rebuilding). The Hermitian eigendecomposition is lazily computed (Eigen SelfAdjointEigenSolver<MatrixXcd>) and cached.

Public Functions

explicit HodgeLaplacian(std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> st)¶

Construct the operator over a triangulation.

Edge weights/phases are read lazily (at the first matrix/spectrum query), so the spacetime must outlive the operator; the held shared_ptr keeps it alive.

std::vector<std::complex<double>> adjacency() const¶

Weighted adjacency \( A \) as a flat row-major \( N\times N \) array of complex entries.

Hermitian by construction.

std::vector<double> degree() const¶

Degree vector \( (D_{00},\dots,D_{N-1,N-1}) \), real, length \( N \) (magnitude convention \( D_{ii} = \sum |\text{squaredLength}| \)).

std::vector<std::complex<double>> laplacian(int k = 0, bool metric = true, bool lorentzian = false) const¶

Laplacian \( L_k \) as a flat row-major matrix of complex entries: \( N\times N \) for \( k = 0 \) ( \( L = D - A \)), else \( |C_k|\times|C_k| \) (the symmetric metric Laplacian above; imaginary parts are zero).

For \( k \geq 1 \), metric = false selects unit weights (the combinatorial Laplacian); metric is ignored at \( k = 0 \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty for \( k \) above the top dimension. With lorentzian = true (and metric, \( k \geq 1 \)) it is instead the signed-weight d’Alembertian assembled directly (generally non-symmetric; the imaginary parts of the returned entries are still zero, the operator being real).

std::vector<double> weights(int k, bool lorentzian = false) const¶

Diagonal inner-product weights \( W_k \) (length \( |C_k| \)) in the canonical ChainComplex column order: the per- \( k \)-simplex Euclidean volume (Simplex::volume, magnitude; degenerate cells fall back to 1 to keep \( W_k \) positive).

\( W_0 = I \) (all ones). Empty for \( k < 0 \) or \( k \) above the top dimension. With lorentzian = true the entries are the signed Simplex::volume() (timelike cells negative; degenerate cells still fall back to \( +1 \) so \( W_k \) stays invertible).

bool isHermitian(double tol = 1e-12) const¶

Whether \( \| L - L^\dagger \| \le \text{tol} \) (Frobenius norm) for the \( k = 0 \) Laplacian.

True by construction.

double unitarityResidual(double t = 1.0) const¶

Unitarity residual of the time-evolution operator \( U = e^{-iLt} = V\,\mathrm{diag}(e^{-i\lambda t})\,V^\dagger \) formed from the eigendecomposition: returns \( \| U U^\dagger - I \| \) (Frobenius).

~0 for the Hermitian \( L \).

Spectrum spectrum(int k = 0, bool metric = true) const¶

The eigendecomposition of \( L_k \) as a Spectrum (real ascending eigenvalues + eigenvectors as Cochains; Spectrum::isHermitian() is true).

The self-adjoint \( k = 0 \) graph Laplacian and the symmetric metric Hodge Laplacian ( \( k \geq 1 \)). For \( k \geq 1 \), metric selects volume vs. unit weights (ignored at \( k = 0 \)). The eigenvectors are indexed over the sorted-id vertex order ( \( k = 0 \)) or the canonical ChainComplex \( k \)-simplex column order ( \( k \geq 1 \)).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

std::vector<double> eigenvalues(int k = 0, bool metric = true) const¶

Eigenvalues of \( L_k \) (real, ascending), a flat view consistent with spectrum(k, metric).

For \( k \geq 1 \), metric selects volume vs. unit weights (ignored at \( k = 0 \)).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

std::vector<std::complex<double>> eigenvectors(int k = 0, bool metric = true) const¶

Eigenvectors of \( L_k \) as a flat row-major \( M\times M \) array ( \( M = N \) for \( k = 0 \), else \( |C_k| \)); column \( j \) (entries at indices \( iM + j \)) is the eigenvector for the \( j \)-th ascending eigenvalue — a flat view consistent with the Cochains of spectrum(k, metric).

For \( k \geq 1 \), metric selects volume vs. unit weights (ignored at \( k = 0 \)).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

std::vector<Cochain> harmonics(int k = 0, double tol = 1e-9, bool metric = true) const¶

Harmonic representatives: the eigenvectors with \( |\lambda| < \text{tol} \) (a basis for \( \ker L_k \cong H_k \), so the count is the harmonic dimension \( = b_k \)), as Cochains over the \( k \)-simplex ordering.

For \( k \geq 1 \), metric selects volume vs. unit weights (ignored at \( k = 0 \)).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

Spectrum lorentzianSpectrum(int k, bool metric = true) const¶

=== Lorentzian (signed-weight) d’Alembertian, \( k \geq 1 \) (§5.6) ===

The eigendecomposition of the signed-weight \( L_k \) (the non-self-adjoint d’Alembertian) as a Spectrum (isHermitian() == false): complex eigenvalues sorted ascending by \( (\mathrm{Re},\mathrm{Im}) \), paired with eigenvectors as Cochains. metric = false falls back to unit weights (the real, nonnegative combinatorial spectrum).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

std::vector<std::complex<double>> lorentzianEigenvalues(int k, bool metric = true) const¶

Eigenvalues of the signed-weight \( L_k \) (the non-self-adjoint d’Alembertian), as complex numbers sorted ascending by \( (\mathrm{Re},\mathrm{Im}) \) — they may be negative or come in complex conjugate pairs.

metric = false falls back to unit weights (positive, so the spectrum is the real combinatorial one). On an all-spacelike complex the spectrum reproduces eigenvalues(k, metric) (real). For \( k = 0 \) this is the signed graph Laplacian \( \partial_1 W_1^{-1}\partial_1^\top \) ( \( W_0 = I \)), distinct from the Hermitian \( k = 0 \) path above.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \). Empty above the top dimension.

std::vector<std::complex<double>> lorentzianEigenvectors(int k, bool metric = true) const¶

Eigenvectors of the signed-weight \( L_k \) as a flat row-major \( M\times M \) complex array; column \( j \) (entries \( iM + j \)) is the eigenvector for the \( j \)-th eigenvalue of lorentzianEigenvalues(k, metric) (same order).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \).

std::vector<Cochain> lorentzianHarmonics(int k, double tol = 1e-9, bool metric = true) const¶

Near-kernel (“harmonic”) representatives of the d’Alembertian: the eigenvectors with \( |\lambda| < \text{tol} \), as Cochains.

For an all-spacelike complex the count is \( b_k \); with genuine timelike cells it can differ (the pseudo-Hodge decomposition). The matching indefinite \( W \)-norms come from lorentzianNullNorms(k, tol, metric) (same order).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \).

std::vector<double> lorentzianNullNorms(int k, double tol = 1e-9, bool metric = true) const¶

The indefinite norms \( \langle h,h\rangle_W = \sum_i W_{k,i}|h_i|^2 \) (signed \( W_k \)) of the near-kernel representatives, one per column of lorentzianHarmonics(k, tol, metric) and in the same order.

A value \( \approx 0 \) flags a null harmonic (a lightlike kernel direction); all entries are positive on an all-spacelike complex.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – for \( k < 0 \).

class DijkgraafWitten¶
#include <DijkgraafWitten.h>

DijkgraafWitten¶

The Dijkgraaf–Witten partition function of a closed oriented triangulated 3-manifold \( W \) with gauge group \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) and a 3-cocycle \( \omega \in Z^3(\mathbb{Z}_2; U(1)) \):

\[ Z(W) = \frac{1}{2^{|V|}} \sum_{\text{flat } g} \prod_{\text{tetrahedra } t} \omega(g_{01}, g_{12}, g_{23})^{\varepsilon_t}. \]
Here \( g \in C^1(W; \mathbb{Z}_2) \) is a flat connection — a value \( g_e \in \{0,1\} \) on each edge with \( (dg)|_\triangle = g_{01} + g_{12} - g_{02} \equiv 0 \pmod 2 \) on every triangle — i.e. an element of \( \ker(d_1 \bmod 2) \), where the coboundary \( d_1 = \partial_2^\top \) is the transpose of ChainComplex::boundaryMatrix(2). \( \varepsilon_t = \pm 1 \) is each tetrahedron’s orientation sign from the fundamental class (ChainComplex::fundamentalClass()), and on an ordered tetrahedron \( [v_0 < v_1 < v_2 < v_3] \) the weight reads the connection on its three “consecutive” edges \( (v_0,v_1), (v_1,v_2), (v_2,v_3) \) — the Alexander–Whitney faces — mapped to their \( C_1 \) (edge) indices.

The sum is the gauge-redundant enumeration over the whole flat space \( \ker(d_1) \) ( \( 2^{\text{nullity}} \) connections, materialized via gf2Span); the division by \( 2^{|V|} \) is the gauge volume, leaving the topological invariant. This brute-force enumeration is intended for the small triangulations on which the invariant is checked by hand; the underlying gf2Span refuses a nullity too large to materialize.

Public Functions

DijkgraafWitten(std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> W, Cocycle w)¶

Build the state sum over a triangulation \( W \) with the chosen cocycle.

\( W \) is read at partitionFunction() time; the held shared_ptr keeps it alive.

std::complex<double> partitionFunction() const¶

The partition function \( Z(W) \in \mathbb{C} \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if \( W \) is null or not a closed oriented 3-manifold (dimension \( \neq 3 \), or no fundamental class), or std::invalid_argument (from gf2Span) if the flat space is too large to enumerate.

std::vector<std::complex<double>> boundaryVector() const¶

The Dijkgraaf–Witten state sum with boundary¶

For a 3-manifold \( W \) with boundary \( \partial W \) the state sum is no longer a scalar but a vector in the boundary Hilbert space \( Z(\partial W) \). Holding the boundary connection \( g|_{\partial W} \) fixed and summing the same tetrahedron product \( \prod_t \omega(g_{01},g_{12},g_{23})^{\varepsilon_t} \) over the interior flat fields produces, for each boundary flat-connection class, a complex amplitude — an element of \( Z(\partial W) \).

Concretely the sum is taken over the bulk cohomology classes \( [g] \in H^1(W;\mathbb{Z}_2) \) (the gauge-inequivalent flat \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) connections — the interior fields modulo gauge), binned by the class of their restriction to each boundary component. A boundary component \( \Sigma \) (a closed surface) carries the DW Hilbert space \( Z(\Sigma) = \mathbb{C}[H^1(\Sigma;\mathbb{Z}_2)] \) of dimension \( 2^{b_1(\Sigma)} \), indexed by the holonomy class of the connection. Summing over cohomology classes (rather than the gauge-redundant cocycle space) is exactly the gauge-fixed “sum over interior fields”; no gauge volume divides it, and it is normalized so the trivial cobordism \( \Sigma\times[0,T] \) is the identity on \( Z(\Sigma) \).

For the real-valued \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \) cocycles (Trivial \( \equiv 1 \) and Sign \( = \pm 1 \)) the orientation exponent is immaterial — \( x^{\pm 1} = x \) for \( x \in \{+1,-1\} \), and \( \omega^{-1} = \bar\omega = \omega \) — so no (relative) fundamental class is needed (none exists for a manifold with boundary) and the product matches the closed case.

boundaryVector() returns the full element of \( Z(\partial W) \): the amplitude for every joint boundary flat-connection class, flattened row-major over the boundary components (each component ordered deterministically by its sorted top-face list). Length \( = \prod_i 2^{b_1(\Sigma_i)} \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if \( W \) is null, not a 3-manifold, or closed (no boundary — use partitionFunction()).

std::vector<int> boundaryDimensions() const¶

The per-boundary-component Hilbert-space dimensions \( 2^{b_1(\Sigma_i)} \), in the same deterministic component order used by boundaryVector() / map().

std::vector<std::vector<std::complex<double>>> map() const¶

The boundary state sum read as a linear map \( Z(\Sigma_B) \to Z(\Sigma_A) \) when \( \partial W \) has exactly two components: a dense matrix returned as rows, rows = 2^{b_1(\Sigma_A)} (component 0), cols = 2^{b_1(\Sigma_B)} (component 1), in the flat-connection-class basis.

For the trivial cobordism \( \Sigma\times[0,T] \) this is the identity \( \mathrm{id}_{Z(\Sigma)} \).

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if \( \partial W \) does not have exactly two connected components.

std::complex<double> amplitude(const PreparedBoundaryState &psiA, const PreparedBoundaryState &psiB) const¶

The transition amplitude \( \langle \psi_A | Z(W) | \psi_B \rangle \) for already-prepared boundary states \( \psi_A \in Z(\Sigma_A) \), \( \psi_B \in Z(\Sigma_B) \) (PreparedBoundaryStates, type-safe — the holonomy-class convention lives in their BoundaryStateSpace, not here): the contraction \( \sum_{a,b} \overline{\psi_A[a]}\, Z(W)_{ab}\, \psi_B[b] \) with the two-component boundary map, reading each state’s coeffs() (the flat-connection-class amplitudes).

For the trivial cobordism ( \( Z(W) = \mathrm{id} \)) this reduces to the inner product \( \langle \psi_A | \psi_B \rangle \); with states prepared from the harmonic 1-forms \( \ker L_1(\Sigma) \) it is the harmonic overlap.

Throws:

std::runtime_error – if \( \partial W \) is not two components, or std::invalid_argument if the state lengths do not match the map dims.

Public Static Functions

static bool isCocycle(Cocycle w)¶

Whether the cocycle \( \omega \) for the given choice satisfies the normalized 3-cocycle (pentagon) identity over \( \mathbb{Z}_2 \): \( \omega(b,c,d)\,\omega(a, b{+}c, d)\,\omega(a,b,c) = \omega(a{+}b, c, d)\,\omega(a, b, c{+}d) \) for every \( (a,b,c,d) \in \mathbb{Z}_2^4 \) (brute-forced over all 16 tuples).

Both Trivial and Sign are genuine cocycles, so both return true; it is the prerequisite that makes the state sum a topological invariant.

class EigenstateSynthesis¶
#include <EigenstateSynthesis.h>

EigenstateSynthesis¶

The §4b inverse eigenvector problem on a fixed complex, degree-parameterized by int k: given a target state \( \psi \), score how close the complex’s current Hermitian edge weights make \( \psi \) to being an eigenvector of the degree- \( k \) Hodge Laplacian \( L_k \) (via HodgeLaplacian), and read/write those weights so a search can perturb them.

At \( k = 0 \) \( L_0 = D - A \) is the U(1)-weighted graph Laplacian (the magnitude convention) and \( \psi \) is a vertex vector (length \( |V| \), sorted-id order). At \( k \geq 1 \) \( L_k \) is the metric Hodge Laplacian on \( k \)-cochains and \( \psi \) is a \( k \)-form (length \( |C_k| \), the canonical ChainComplex \( k \)-cell order); the tunable parameters stay the edge squared-lengths (Edge::setSquaredLength), which feed the per-simplex volume weights \( W_k \) of \( L_k \) through Simplex::volume (the U(1) phases enter only the \( k = 0 \) operator). This lifts the §5.0 fixed-boundary interior fill from the \( k = 0 \) 2-complex setting to the \( k = 1 \) boundary harmonic of a 3-manifold-with-boundary (#176): a 3-manifold \( W \) whose \( \ker L_1(\partial W) \) is matched by pinning \( \partial W \) and filling the interior. cellSimplices() gives the sorted vertex-id tuple of each \( \psi \) component, so a caller can pin the boundary \( k \)-cells to a target form and leave the interior free.

The search itself (non-convex, multi-restart, e.g. scipy.optimize.minimize L-BFGS-B over the flat \( \{w_{ij}\}\cup\{\theta_{ij}\} \) vector) drives the cone-and-retry growth loop in a separate stage; this class is the residual + parameter access core it calls. Growing the complex (coning-in auxiliary vertices) is out of scope here.

Residual¶

For a unit target \( \psi \) the eigenvalue-agnostic residual is the squared norm of the component of \( L\psi \) orthogonal to \( \psi \), \( r(\psi) = \big\|\,(I-\psi\psi^\dagger)\,L\,\psi\,\big\|^2 = \|L\psi - \lambda\psi\|^2,\quad \lambda = \psi^\dagger L\psi, \) so \( r = 0 \iff L\psi \parallel \psi \iff \psi \) is an eigenvector, and the realized eigenvalue is the Rayleigh quotient \( \lambda \). A non-unit \( \psi \) is normalized internally (the eigenvector condition is scale-invariant). The Laplacian is reassembled from the current edge weights/phases on every call, so the residual tracks in-place perturbations of setWeights / setPhases.

Parameters¶

The tunable parameters are the per-edge squared-length magnitudes \( \{w_{ij}\} \) (Edge::setSquaredLength) and U(1) connection phases \( \{\theta_{ij}\} \) (Edge::setPhase), in a stable edge order fixed at construction (the EdgeList order, restricted to the edges that carry weight in \( L \): both endpoints present, no self-loops). weights() / phases() read them; setWeights() / setPhases() write them back in place — no mesh rebuild. psi components are indexed in the same sorted-vertex-id order as HodgeLaplacian ( \( k=0 \)), so they align with the operator.

Fixed-boundary interior fill (§5.0)¶

The realizability oracle (#138) fills the interior of a bulk \( W_{AB} \) whose boundary is pinned — the §4b cone-and-retry restricted to the interior. The tunable edges split into the boundary set \( \partial W \) (those on a codimension-one face belonging to exactly one top cell — held fixed) and the interior set (everything else — free). interiorWeights() / interiorPhases() and setInteriorWeights() / setInteriorPhases() read/write only the interior edges, so a search drives \( r\to 0 \) for a target output eigenvector while \( \partial W \) stays byte-identical; boundaryEdges() exposes that fixed set for verification. growInterior() cones a fresh interior vertex into a top cell via the boundary-fixed pre-geometric Pachner add (#112) — a topology-preserving \( 1\!\to\!(d+1) \) stellar subdivision that enriches the interior with \( \partial W \) untouched — and re-captures the partition, so the loop can optimize, then grow, then re-optimize. interiorVertexCount() / numInteriorEdges() report the interior complexity reached: a reachable target drives \( r\to 0 \) at some minimal complexity, an unreachable one floors at a positive residual (the spectral obstruction the oracle consumes). The boundary edge classification needs genuine codim-one structure (top cells of \( \ge 3 \) vertices); on a pure 1-complex every edge is interior (the free §4b regime).

bool growInterior(std::uint64_t seed)¶

Cone a fresh interior vertex into a top cell via the boundary-fixed pre-geometric Pachner add (#112): a \( 1\!\to\!(d+1) \) stellar subdivision (valid in any dimension — \( 1\!\to\!4 \) on a tetrahedron in 3D) that leaves \( \partial W \) exactly fixed while enriching the interior.

Re-captures the \( k \)-cell order (cellSimplices()), tunable edges, and interior/boundary partition, so order() and numInteriorEdges() grow. At \( k = 0 \) the new apex is the largest id, appended last, so existing psi indices are preserved; at \( k \geq 1 \) the new \( k \)-cells interleave in the canonical order, so re-identify the boundary/interior components via cellSimplices() (by sorted vertex-id tuple) after each grow. The RNG seed makes the target-cell choice reproducible. Returns false if no top cell can be subdivided (e.g. a 1-complex, top cells of \( <3 \) vertices), leaving the complex unchanged.

bool attachInteriorVertex(const std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> &incidentSimplices)¶

Add a fresh interior vertex with an arbitrary specified set of incident simplices — the cone-free generalization of growInterior.

Each entry of incidentSimplices is a set of existing vertex ids; the new vertex together with that set forms one new simplex, whose 1-skeleton (every pairwise edge) is materialized. So a singleton entry \( \{u\} \) wires the new vertex to \( u \) by an edge, and the \( d \) facets of a top cell reproduce that cell’s cone connectivity — coning is one special case.

The new vertex takes the largest id (it appends last in sorted-id order, so the boundary-support \( \psi \) prefix is preserved). The move is purely additive (nothing is removed) and validates only the two invariants the experiment allows: (a) the result is a valid downward-closed abstract simplicial complex (every pair within each new simplex carries an edge), and (b) the pinned boundary \( \partial W \) is bit-exact untouched (same edge set, same weights/phases). No manifold / pseudomanifold / orientability / purity / topology constraint is imposed. Re-captures the operator and the interior/boundary partition.

Returns false, leaving the complex unchanged (rolled back), if a spec is empty, references a missing vertex, repeats a vertex, or the attach would perturb \( \partial W \). Because only the k=0 graph Laplacian’s edges feed residual(), wiring the interior vertex by edges (singleton specs) is always boundary-safe: a new edge to a brand-new vertex creates no new top cell and changes no facet count among the pinned boundary.

bool detachLastInteriorVertex()¶

Undo the most recent attachInteriorVertex (LIFO): remove the simplices and edges it created and the interior vertex it added, restoring the complex bit-exactly, and re-capture.

Returns false if there is no attach to undo. Lets a connectivity search try a candidate, score it, and roll back to try the next.

std::vector<std::uint64_t> vertexIds() const¶

All vertex ids in the complex, sorted ascending — the candidate pool a connectivity search wires a fresh interior vertex into.

std::vector<std::uint64_t> boundaryVertexIds() const¶

The boundary ( \( \partial W \)) vertex ids, sorted ascending — the vertices on a codim-one face of exactly one top cell.

A “boundary-star” connectivity candidate wires the new vertex to these.

std::vector<std::vector<std::uint64_t>> topCells() const¶

The top cells as sorted vertex-id tuples (the \( d+1 \)-vertex simplices).

The “cone-equivalent” connectivity candidate wires the new vertex to one of these cells’ vertices, reproducing growInterior’s 1-skeleton.

struct CharacteristicNumbers¶
#include <Characteristic.h>

Characteristic numbers (Capability A)¶

A bundle of topological invariants of a closed PL \( n \)-manifold. The invariants that are a single number (Euler characteristic, signature) are also available individually as Observables above; this struct additionally carries the ones that are families of numbers (Stiefel–Whitney and Pontryagin numbers).

Public Members

int euler = {0}¶

Euler characteristic (see EulerCharacteristic above).

std::optional<int> signature = {}¶

Signature (see Signature above).

Present only for an orientable 4-manifold; left empty for a non-orientable 4-manifold or any dimension other than 4, where it is not defined.

std::map<std::string, int> stiefelWhitneyNumbers = {}¶

Stiefel–Whitney numbers: a family of yes/no (mod-2) invariants that detect orientability and related “twisting” of the manifold.

Each entry is keyed by the characteristic-class monomial it comes from (for example the key “w1^2” is the number obtained from the first Stiefel–Whitney class squared), with value in \( \{0, 1\} \).

Note

Not computed yet — pending the Stiefel–Whitney / Wu-class work; the map is currently always empty.

std::map<std::string, long> pontryaginNumbers = {}¶

Pontryagin numbers: integer invariants coming from curvature, defined for orientable manifolds whose dimension is a multiple of 4.

In dimension 4 there is only one, conventionally keyed “p1”, and the Hirzebruch signature theorem says it equals three times the signature ( \( \langle p_1, [K]\rangle = 3\sigma \)).

Public Static Functions

static CharacteristicNumbers of(const Spacetime &K, bool oriented = true)¶

Compute the characteristic numbers of the manifold K.

For an orientable 4-manifold this fills in the signature and the Pontryagin number \( p_1 = 3\sigma \). The oriented flag will later select which invariants to report (orientation-dependent ones vs. the mod-2 Stiefel–Whitney numbers) once those are implemented.

class EulerCharacteristic : public Observable¶
#include <Characteristic.h>

EulerCharacteristic¶

Observable measuring the Euler characteristic of a triangulation: the alternating count of its cells, \( \chi = (\text{vertices}) - (\text{edges}) + (\text{triangles}) - \cdots = \sum_{k} (-1)^k\, |C_k| \). It is one of the most basic topological invariants — two triangulations of the same shape always give the same value (for example every triangulation of a 2-sphere has \( \chi = 2 \)). Computed from the chain complex’s face counts.

Public Functions

double compute(const std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> &spacetime) override¶
class Signature : public Observable¶
#include <Characteristic.h>

Signature¶

Observable measuring the signature of a closed, orientable 4-dimensional manifold. The manifold’s two-dimensional “holes” carry a symmetric pairing (the intersection form): given two such holes it returns an integer counting how they cross. The signature is \( \sigma = (\text{number of positive directions}) - (\text{number of negative directions}) \) of that pairing — equivalently the count of positive minus negative eigenvalues. It is what tells apart manifolds that share the same Euler characteristic and homology (and is the key to telling two different fillings of the same boundary apart).

Returns 0 when there are no two-dimensional holes, or when the manifold is not 4-dimensional. See :func:ChainComplex::signature.

class CombinatorialDimension : public Observable¶
#include <CombinatorialDimension.h>

CombinatorialDimension¶

Observable: the combinatorial dimension of a triangulation — the largest \( k \) for which a \( k \)-simplex is present (the maximum simplex vertex count minus one), or \( -1 \) for the empty complex.

This is a purely combinatorial/topological quantity: an exact integer equal to \( n \) for a clean PL \( n \)-manifold triangulation, fixed by the simplex set alone. It is not the spectral dimension (Spacetime::getSpectralDimensionOnSkeleton), which is a real-valued, scale-dependent diffusion quantity that can differ from \( n \) (dimensional reduction); nor the Hausdorff (volume-scaling) dimension. It is also distinct from the metric’s declared dimension: a hand-assembled lower-dimensional triangulation (e.g. a surface \( S^2 \)) can live inside a 4D-signature Spacetime.

The cobordism capabilities key their dimension-dependent logic off this integer (the existence table is indexed by \( n \in \{0,1,2,3,4\} \), the signature is defined only for \( n=4 \), vertex links must be \( (n-1) \)-spheres, …) — a role a real-valued spectral dimension cannot fill.

Implemented as an :class:Observable (returning the dimension as a double) following tessera’s convention for scalar measurements of a triangulation. The characteristic-number capabilities (Euler characteristic, signature, …) are likewise Observables; multi-complex / structural operations (cobordism verification, reconstruction, Pachner search) are static-only classes.

class ChoiJamiolkowski¶
#include <ChoiJamiolkowski.h>

Dense Choi–Jamiołkowski map–state duality (“bending”).

A stateless static-only utility (the cobordism::Cobordism pattern): not instantiable, every operation is a static method. All matrices/vectors are flat, row-major std::vector<std::complex<double>> (see the file header for the locked conventions); Eigen is used internally for the SVD.

Public Functions

ChoiJamiolkowski() = delete¶

Public Static Functions

static std::vector<std::complex<double>> vectorize(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, int dA, int dB)¶

Vectorise a dA×dB operator: vec(U) = Σ_{ij} U_{ij} |i⟩_A ⊗ |j⟩_B.

With the row-major convention the tensor index is i*dB + j, so vec(U) is exactly the row-major flatten of U (length dA·dB). Throws std::invalid_argument if U.size() != dA·dB or a dimension is non-positive.

static std::vector<double> singularValues(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, int dA, int dB)¶

Singular values of the dA×dB operator U (Eigen JacobiSVD), in descending order; min(dA, dB) of them.

These are the Schmidt coefficients of vec(U).

static int schmidtRank(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, int dA, int dB, double tol = 1e-10)¶

Schmidt rank of vec(U): the number of singular values of U that exceed tol·σ_max (σ_max the largest singular value).

Equals the operator rank of U and the bipartite Schmidt rank of the state vec(U).

static std::vector<std::complex<double>> transitionOperator(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &psiA, const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &psiB, int dA, int dB)¶

Transition operator U_T = |psiA⟩⟨psiB| (a rank-one dA×dB matrix, (U_T)_{ij} = psiA_i · conj(psiB_j)), returned flat row-major.

Throws std::invalid_argument if psiA.size() != dA or psiB.size() != dB.

static std::complex<double> transitionAmplitude(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &psiA, const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &psiB, int dA, int dB)¶

Transition amplitude ⟨psiA|U|psiB⟩ = Σ_{ij} conj(psiA_i)·U_{ij}·psiB_j.

By the duality identity this equals ⟨vec(U_T)|vec(U)⟩ = Tr(U_T^H·U) for U_T = |psiA⟩⟨psiB|. Throws std::invalid_argument on a dimension mismatch.

static std::vector<std::complex<double>> choiState(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, int d)¶

Choi–Jamiołkowski state of a square d×d operator U: the maximally- entangled bend |Φ_U⟩ = (U ⊗ I)|Φ⁺⟩ with |Φ⁺⟩ = (1/√d) Σ_k |k⟩|k⟩, which in the row-major convention is the normalised vec, (1/√d)·vec(U) (length d·d).

For unitary U this is a unit vector. Throws std::invalid_argument if U.size() != d·d or d is non-positive.

static std::vector<std::complex<double>> choiMatrix(const std::vector<std::complex<double>> &U, int d)¶

Choi matrix J(U) = |Φ_U⟩⟨Φ_U| of a square d×d operator U: the (d·d)×(d·d) density matrix of choiState(U, d), returned flat row-major (J[i·d² + j] = state_i · conj(state_j)).

This is the standard (U ⊗ I)|Φ⁺⟩⟨Φ⁺|(U ⊗ I)^H Choi matrix; Tr J = 1 for unitary U. Throws std::invalid_argument as choiState.

class KoashiImotoBlock¶
#include <KoashiImoto.hpp>

One classical block of a Koashi-Imoto decomposition.

In the symmetric KI form ρ_AB = ⊕_j p_j · ρ_{A_L B_L,j} ⊗ ω_{A_R,j} ⊗ ω_{B_R,j}, this stores the j-th summand: its weight p_j, the joint core state on the left blocks (coreState), the per-side right-tail states (tailA, tailB), and the four block dimensions.

Constructed by koashiImotoDecompose; immutable after build (callers should treat instances as read-only outputs).

class KoashiImotoTolerances¶
#include <KoashiImoto.hpp>

Numerical tolerances used by koashiImotoDecompose.

The KI algorithm does several rank-detection / eigendecomposition steps. Each step has its own conditioning threshold, separated so callers can dial them independently when chasing edge cases (in practice they all sit at ~1e-10 for double precision).

double vanRaamsdonkDistanceTo(const ::tessera::mesh::Vertex *other, double iMax) const¶

Compute the Van Raamsdonk distance d_VR = −log(I / iMax) between this vertex and other.

I is the mutual information of the bipartite product joint ρ_this ⊗ ρ_other, so this method gives the correct d_VR for any pair that has no inherited correlation (which is every pair the KI factories build except the input (A, B) edge). Two product marginals have I = 0, so the returned distance is +∞ except in trivial cases.

The KI-cell factory uses this method for the nine non-(A, B) edges and computes the (A, B) edge separately from its input joint ρ_AB. The factory then writes d_VR² into Edge::squaredLength (the canonical edge length-property field).

other must be a QuantumVertex — throws otherwise.

class MatterConfiguration¶
#include <MatterConfiguration.h>

Intrinsic (coordinate-free) specification of stress-energy on a triangulation.

For point particles, the matter action is the proper-time action: \(S_{\text{matter}} = -M \int d\tau = -M \sum_{e \in \text{worldline}} \sqrt{-\ell^2_e}\)

The Regge equations \(\partial S/\partial \ell^2_e = 0\) then give the discrete Einstein equations sourced by the particle.

Public Functions

void setWorldlineMass(VertexPtr center, double mass, const Spacetime &st)¶

Assign a static point mass along its worldline through all time slices.

Traces a worldline from center through the foliation by following timelike edges, then stores the worldline for the proper-time action.

Public Static Functions

static std::vector<VertexPtr> buildWorldline(VertexPtr center, const Spacetime &st)¶

Trace a worldline through all time slices, passing through the spatial center of each slice.

Returns one vertex per slice, ordered by time.

On each slice, the center vertex is the one with the most spacelike neighbors. Ties are broken by BFS (depth <= 5) sum-of-distances. The depth limit avoids wrapping around compact topologies.

namespace spacetime

Constraints¶

namespace tessera

Enums

enum class ConstraintType : uint8_t¶

Types of constraints that can be applied to a spacetime.

  • PachnerMove: Constraints specific to a proposed Pachner move (e.g., checking that a bistellar flip preserves the manifold condition).

  • All: Global constraints that must hold at all times (e.g., the simplicial complex must remain a manifold, the causal structure must be preserved).

Values:

enumerator PachnerMove¶
enumerator All¶
class Constraint¶
#include <Constraint.h>

Constraint Base Class¶

Encodes conditions that a spacetime triangulation must satisfy. In CDT, the central constraint is causality: every \( d \)-simplex must have its vertices distributed across exactly two adjacent time slices, preserving the global time foliation. This ensures that each spatial slice is a closed \((d\!-\!1)\)-manifold and that the causal structure is well-defined.

Additional constraints may include:

  • Manifoldness: every \((d\!-\!1)\)-face is shared by at most 2 \( d \)-simplices (the link of every simplex is a sphere).

  • Topology preservation: Pachner moves must not change the topology of the spatial slices or the overall manifold.

  • Volume bounds: the total four-volume \( N_4 \) must remain within a specified range during the simulation.

Public Functions

virtual ~Constraint() = default¶
virtual bool applies(const std::shared_ptr<Spacetime> &spacetime, const ConstraintType &type_) = 0¶

Check whether a constraint is satisfied for the current spacetime state.

Parameters:

  • spacetime – The spacetime to check

  • type_ – The type of constraint check to perform

Returns:

true if the constraint is satisfied

GPU / CUDA acceleration¶

namespace tessera
namespace cuda¶

Functions

void compute_deficits_gpu(const GpuMeshData &mesh, double *h_deficits)¶

Compute deficit angles for all hinges on the GPU.

void compute_gradients_gpu(const GpuMeshData &mesh, double *h_gradients)¶

Compute numerical gradients of the deficit-residual Σ(ε_h - ε_target)² for all edges in parallel on the GPU.

void compute_action_gradient_gpu(const GpuMeshData &mesh, double *h_gradients)¶

Compute the action gradient ∂S/∂ℓ²_e for all edges in parallel, where S = Σ A_h·ε_h + S_matter.

This is the correct gradient for the Regge equation solver’s step() function.

void compute_step_gpu(const GpuMeshData &mesh, double *h_base_grad, double *h_dF)¶

Compute one full solver step on the GPU:

  1. Base action gradient ∂S/∂W_e (1 kernel launch)

  2. Fused ∂F/∂W_e where F = ||∇S||² (1 kernel launch) All GPU memory is allocated once, uploaded once, downloaded once. h_base_grad[n_edges] receives ∂S/∂W_e. h_dF[n_edges] receives ∂F/∂W_e.

Variables

constexpr int MAX_DIM = 8¶

Maximum Cayley-Menger matrix dimension (d+2 for d-simplices).

For 4D CDT: 5 vertices → 6×6 bordered matrix. Extra margin for safety.

struct GpuMeshData¶
#include <regge_cuda.h>

Flattened mesh topology for GPU computation.

All connectivity is encoded as CSR (Compressed Sparse Row) arrays so the GPU can traverse the mesh without pointer chasing.
